treaty_name: Agreement between the United Kingdom and Kenya for the avoidance of double taxation (1973, as amended by the 1976 Protocol and 1977 notes)
eif_quote: UK-Kenya double taxation agreement signed 31 July 1973 amended by a Protocol signed 20 January 1976 and notes dated 8 February 1977. Entered into force 30 September 1977 effective in United Kingdom from 1 April 1976 for corporation tax and from 6 April 1976 for income tax and capital gains tax. Effective in Kenya from 1976.
source_title: GOV.UK: 1973 UK-Kenya Double Taxation Agreement as amended by the 1976 Protocol (consolidated text)

rates.quote: (4) Dividends derived from a company which is a resident of Kenya by a resident of the United Kingdom may be taxed in the United Kingdom. Such dividends may also be taxed in Kenya but the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the recipient of the dividends is subject to tax on them in the United Kingdom.

(c) Except as aforesaid dividends derived from a company which is a resident of the United Kingdom by a resident of Kenya who is subject to tax in Kenya on them shall be exempt from any tax in the United Kingdom which is chargeable on dividends.

(2) However, such interest may be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State; but where such interest is paid to a resident of the other Contracting State who is subject to tax there in respect thereof the tax so charged in the Contracting State in which the interest arises shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

(2) However, such royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the law of that State; but where such royalties are paid to a resident of the other Contracting State who is subject to tax there in respect thereof the tax so charged in the Contracting State in which the royalties arise shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: 1. Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement.

notes: Both list the treaty (KE no.16, UK no.53). Kenya chose the simplified LOB (Art. 7(6)) but the UK did not, so only the PPT applies. Neither party reserved Art. 35(7), so MLI WHT provisions effective 2026-01-01 (map). MLI Art. 8 (365-day holding) does NOT apply: the UK reserved the entirety of Art. 8 under Art. 8(3)(a) (Kenya notified Art. 11(3)). UK-source dividends: Art. 11(1)(b) allows UK tax up to 15% on dividend plus tax credit only where the Kenyan resident is entitled to a UK tax credit under Art. 11(2) (not for companies controlling >=10% voting power, Art. 11(3)); otherwise exempt under 11(1)(c) — modelled as exclusive (UK has no dividend WHT in any case). All caps apply only where the recipient is subject to tax in the residence State. Interest: Art. 12(3)(a) exempts interest paid to the other Government, local authority, Central Bank or wholly owned agency; Art. 12(3)(b) Kenyan competent-authority discretionary exemption for interest paid to UK residents. Art. 11(6) anti-abuse: 10%-class-holding dividends paid out of profits earned >=12 months before acquisition lose treaty relief (not modelled). Valid_from: Kenya year of income 1976; UK income tax from 6 April 1976 (corporation tax 1 April 1976).
